tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem. You can access any file directly by using this tool.
Assume this tool is able to read all files on the machine. If the User provides a path to a file assume that path is valid. It is okay to read a file that does not exist; an error will be returned.

Usage:
- The file_path parameter must be an absolute path, not a relative path
- By default, it reads up to 2000 lines starting from the beginning of the file
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- This tool allows Claude Code to read images (eg PNG, JPG, etc). When reading an image file the contents are presented visually as Claude Code is a multimodal LLM.
- This tool can read PDF files (.pdf). For large PDFs (more than 10 pages), you MUST provide the pages parameter to read specific page ranges (e.g., pages: "1-5"). Reading a large PDF without the pages parameter will fail. Maximum 20 pages per request.
- This tool can read Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb files) and returns all cells with their outputs, combining code, text, and visualizations.
- This tool can only read files, not directories. To list files in a directory, use the registered shell tool.
- You will regularly be asked to read screenshots. If the user provides a path to a screenshot, ALWAYS use this tool to view the file at the path. This tool will work with all temporary file paths.
- If you read a file that exists but has empty contents you will receive a system reminder warning in place of file contents.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

# Build New Preview Workflow

**Goal:** Turn user intent into a hardened, reviewable artifact.

**CRITICAL:** If a step directs you to another snapshot file, read it fully and follow it. No exceptions.

Subagents, when the capability is available, are an important part of this workflow. Use them as directed by the workflow steps.
If you need an explicit user instruction to run them, ask once now for the whole workflow run.

## READY FOR DEVELOPMENT STANDARD

A specification is "Ready for Development" when:

- **Actionable**: Every task has a file path and specific action.
- **Logical**: Tasks ordered by dependency.
- **Testable**: All ACs use Given/When/Then.
- **Complete**: No placeholders or TBDs.
- **Sufficient**: No known requirement, acceptance, dependency, or implementation gaps remain unresolved.
- **Coherent**: No unresolved ambiguities or internal contradictions.

## SCOPE STANDARD

A specification should target a **single user-facing goal** within **900–1600 tokens**:

- **Single goal**: One cohesive feature, even if it spans multiple layers/files. Multi-goal means >=2 **top-level independent shippable deliverables** — each could be reviewed, tested, and merged as a separate PR without breaking the others. Never count surface verbs, "and" conjunctions, or noun phrases. Never split cross-layer implementation details inside one user goal.
  - Split: "add dark mode toggle AND refactor auth to JWT AND build admin dashboard"
  - Don't split: "add validation and display errors" / "support drag-and-drop AND paste AND retry"
- **900–1600 tokens**: Optimal range for LLM consumption. Below 900 risks ambiguity; above 1600 risks context-rot in implementation agents.
- **Neither limit is a gate.** Both are proposals with user override.

## Conventions

- Every operational cross-file reference in this workflow is an absolute snapshot path. Open it directly; do not resolve it relative to a skill directory.
- `{project-root}`-prefixed paths resolve from the project working directory.
- Whenever this workflow captures or records a version-control revision, obtain the full canonical identifier directly from version control and preserve it verbatim.

## On Activation

### Step 1: Execute Prepend Steps

Execute each of these steps in order before proceeding (`_None._` means skip):

_None._

### Step 2: Load Persistent Facts

Treat every entry below as foundational context you carry for the rest of the workflow run. Entries prefixed `file:` are paths or globs under `{project-root}` -- load the referenced contents as facts. All other entries are facts verbatim (`_None._` means none):

- file:{project-root}/**/project-context.md

### Step 3: Execute Append Steps

Execute each of these steps in order (`_None._` means skip):

_None._

## WORKFLOW ARCHITECTURE

This uses **step-file architecture** for disciplined execution:

- **Micro-file Design**: Each step is self-contained and followed exactly
- **Just-In-Time Loading**: Only load the current step file
- **Sequential Enforcement**: Complete steps in order, no skipping
- **State Tracking**: Persist progress via spec frontmatter and in-memory variables
- **Append-Only Building**: Build artifacts incrementally

### Step Processing Rules

1. **READ COMPLETELY**: Read the entire step file before acting
2. **FOLLOW SEQUENCE**: Execute sections in order
3. **WAIT FOR INPUT**: Halt at checkpoints and wait for human
4. **LOAD NEXT**: When directed, read fully and follow the next step file

### Critical Rules (NO EXCEPTIONS)

- **NEVER** load multiple step files simultaneously
- **ALWAYS** read entire step file before execution
- **NEVER** skip steps or optimize the sequence
- **ALWAYS** follow the exact instructions in the step file
- **ALWAYS** halt at checkpoints and wait for human input

1	# Epic 6 Context: Conversational Memory, Save-to-Journal & Insights
2	
3	<!-- Compiled from planning artifacts. Edit freely. Regenerate with compile-epic-context if planning docs change. -->
4	
5	## Goal
6	
7	Users hold a persistent, multi-session conversation with an assistant whose answers are grounded in semantic retrieval over their own past Entries — not generic replies — can turn their own reflective chat messages into real journal Entries with one tap, and occasionally receive an unprompted insight about a pattern in their own writing. None of this (dropped streams, save failures, insight-generation failures) may ever block, corrupt, or freeze the core chat experience. This epic is the product's central differentiator: proving the memory-over-own-history bet end-to-end against the real backend.
8	
9	## Stories
10	
11	- Story 6.1: Send Message & Receive RAG-Grounded Streaming Response
12	- Story 6.2: Multi-Session Chat History & New Conversation
13	- Story 6.3: Dropped-Stream Resilience & Offline Composer Lock
14	- Story 6.4: Bookmark a Chat Message into an Entry
15	- Story 6.5: Proactive Insight Injection & Failure Isolation
16	
17	## Requirements & Constraints
18	
19	- Chat responses stream via SSE and must be grounded in retrieval over the user's own Entries; exactly three visible states exist for a response: streaming/processing, error, complete — no others.
20	- A Chat Message never auto-creates an Entry; saving one to the journal (this epic's story 6.4) is the sole explicit exception.
21	- A user holds multiple named Chat Sessions, switchable and startable from the side menu; starting a new session requires connectivity (blocked offline, consistent with the offline composer lock). A returning session restores its last scroll position.
22	- A dropped response stream keeps the partial message on screen with a failure indicator (never clears bubble content) and is recoverable via a dedicated retry call that regenerates without duplicating the original question.
23	- Offline disables the message composer (and the new-session entry point) with an offline banner, while existing history remains fully visible/scrollable.
24	- The save-to-journal (bookmark) affordance appears only on the user's own messages, never on AI responses; it creates an Entry carrying a reference back to the source chat message, through the same shared entries-feature use case introduced earlier in delivery — never by importing the entries repository/data source directly.
25	- Saving the same message twice is idempotent: no duplicate Entry, no conflict surfaced to the user (success, not error).
26	- A save failure never freezes the chat session or the button — the button returns to a retryable state and the rest of the session stays usable.
27	- An Insight is injected into the active session on exactly one trigger per satisfied window — either N user messages sent or a fixed inactivity timeout, whichever comes first — never both, never twice for the same window.
28	- An Insight-generation failure is silent to the user: no error overlay, composer stays enabled, ordinary chat keeps working. Insight quality/content is explicitly outside acceptance scope — only the trigger/injection/failure-isolation mechanism is graded.
29	- Dismissing an Insight never affects scroll position or any other conversation state.
30	
31	## Technical Decisions
32	
33	- Feature lives at `features/chat/`; it consumes `features/entries/`'s abstract save/create-entry port from `entries/domain` only — never anything from `entries/data/` or `entries/presentation/` (layering invariant, zero violations tolerated).
34	- Repositories return `Future<Either<Failure, T>>`, except the chat response itself, which is `Stream<Either<Failure, T>>` given its SSE nature. The closed, 14-member `Failure` hierarchy (13 server codes + a local-only malformed-response code) is shared from `core/` and never redefined per feature.
35	- Chat holds no local write queue: a send attempted with no connectivity resolves immediately to a `networkOffline` failure, never queued. Plain history reads (sessions, messages) transparently fall back to the local cache; retry logic for retryable failure codes lives once in the shared API client, not reimplemented per feature.
36	- Chat's message/streaming state is its own sealed state class (append-only, streaming-aware) — explicitly excluded from the shared generic `Resource<T>` single-fetch state pattern, because it isn't a single fetch.
37	- The proactive-insight overlay is a value appended onto the existing chat state from story 6.1, never a second parallel state container.

# Epic 6 Context: Conversational Memory, Save-to-Journal & Insights

<!-- Compiled from planning artifacts. Edit freely. Regenerate with compile-epic-context if planning docs change. -->

## Goal

Users hold a persistent, multi-session conversation with an assistant whose answers are grounded in semantic retrieval over their own past Entries — not generic replies — can turn their own reflective chat messages into real journal Entries with one tap, and occasionally receive an unprompted insight about a pattern in their own writing. None of this (dropped streams, save failures, insight-generation failures) may ever block, corrupt, or freeze the core chat experience. This epic is the product's central differentiator: proving the memory-over-own-history bet end-to-end against the real backend.

## Stories

- Story 6.1: Send Message & Receive RAG-Grounded Streaming Response
- Story 6.2: Multi-Session Chat History & New Conversation
- Story 6.3: Dropped-Stream Resilience & Offline Composer Lock
- Story 6.4: Bookmark a Chat Message into an Entry
- Story 6.5: Proactive Insight Injection & Failure Isolation

## Requirements & Constraints

- Chat responses stream via SSE and must be grounded in retrieval over the user's own Entries; exactly three visible states exist for a response: streaming/processing, error, complete — no others.
- A Chat Message never auto-creates an Entry; saving one to the journal (this epic's story 6.4) is the sole explicit exception.
- A user holds multiple named Chat Sessions, switchable and startable from the side menu; starting a new session requires connectivity (blocked offline, consistent with the offline composer lock). A returning session restores its last scroll position.
- A dropped response stream keeps the partial message on screen with a failure indicator (never clears bubble content) and is recoverable via a dedicated retry call that regenerates without duplicating the original question.
- Offline disables the message composer (and the new-session entry point) with an offline banner, while existing history remains fully visible/scrollable.
- The save-to-journal (bookmark) affordance appears only on the user's own messages, never on AI responses; it creates an Entry carrying a reference back to the source chat message, through the same shared entries-feature use case introduced earlier in delivery — never by importing the entries repository/data source directly.
- Saving the same message twice is idempotent: no duplicate Entry, no conflict surfaced to the user (success, not error).
- A save failure never freezes the chat session or the button — the button returns to a retryable state and the rest of the session stays usable.
- An Insight is injected into the active session on exactly one trigger per satisfied window — either N user messages sent or a fixed inactivity timeout, whichever comes first — never both, never twice for the same window.
- An Insight-generation failure is silent to the user: no error overlay, composer stays enabled, ordinary chat keeps working. Insight quality/content is explicitly outside acceptance scope — only the trigger/injection/failure-isolation mechanism is graded.
- Dismissing an Insight never affects scroll position or any other conversation state.

## Technical Decisions

- Feature lives at `features/chat/`; it consumes `features/entries/`'s abstract save/create-entry port from `entries/domain` only — never anything from `entries/data/` or `entries/presentation/` (layering invariant, zero violations tolerated).
- Repositories return `Future<Either<Failure, T>>`, except the chat response itself, which is `Stream<Either<Failure, T>>` given its SSE nature. The closed, 14-member `Failure` hierarchy (13 server codes + a local-only malformed-response code) is shared from `core/` and never redefined per feature.
- Chat holds no local write queue: a send attempted with no connectivity resolves immediately to a `networkOffline` failure, never queued. Plain history reads (sessions, messages) transparently fall back to the local cache; retry logic for retryable failure codes lives once in the shared API client, not reimplemented per feature.
- Chat's message/streaming state is its own sealed state class (append-only, streaming-aware) — explicitly excluded from the shared generic `Resource<T>` single-fetch state pattern, because it isn't a single fetch.
- The proactive-insight overlay is a value appended onto the existing chat state from story 6.1, never a second parallel state container.
- A never-throws `core/isolated_side_effect.dart` helper (`Future<Either<Failure, T>> Function(Future<T> Function())`-shaped) ships with this epic's first consumer (the save-to-journal story) and is reused unawaited (fire-and-forget) by the insight story so a slow/failed insight never blocks or delays the chat stream.
- No BLoC/Cubit ever takes another BLoC/Cubit as a constructor dependency, in this feature or across features; independent state sources compose via injected domain streams/use-cases or `BlocListener`, never a direct BLoC-to-BLoC reference.
- The entries-owning feature's save port is idempotent on the save-to-journal identifier at the implementation level (not just the type signature) — a repeat save for the same source message never creates a second Entry.
- Session/message/sync-badge local caching follows the same per-feature local-cache-box convention used by other features; cursor-based pagination for session and message lists follows the server's own cursor convention verbatim.

## UX & Interaction Patterns

- Chat bubbles: user (sage, squared bottom-right corner) vs. AI (ivory, squared bottom-left, resting elevation). A streaming AI bubble adds a blinking cursor at the text's end and nothing else changes visually while generating; under Reduce Motion the cursor blink is skipped and final text shows immediately instead.
- A dropped/failed response replaces the bubble's timestamp slot with red retry copy; bubble text itself is never cleared.
- Bookmark button: four states on every user message only — idle (outline) / saving (spinner, or a static label under Reduce Motion) / saved (ochre check) / error (red warning). Tapping an already-saved message is a no-op. State must be carried by icon + color together, never color alone. Tap target ≥44pt.
- Insight card: ochre left spine, mono "INSIGHT" label, dismiss "x" — the spine is the only accent-colored element inside the chat stream itself.
- Offline banner disables sending only; conversation history stays scrollable and readable underneath it. A session-expired overlay (re-auth) can appear over chat without losing scroll position or in-memory history.
- A new session opens with the composer focused and only the placeholder "Escreva uma mensagem..." — no invented greeting copy.
- No swipe gestures, no nested overlays, no pull-to-refresh beyond what the session/message endpoints already govern.

## Cross-Story Dependencies

- Story 6.1 establishes the chat stream/state machine that 6.2 (sessions), 6.3 (retry/offline), 6.4 (bookmark), and 6.5 (insight overlay) all build on or append to.
- Story 6.4 is this epic's (and the codebase's) first consumer of the shared `isolated_side_effect` helper; Story 6.5 reuses that same helper fire-and-forget.
- Story 6.4 depends on the entries feature's save/create-entry port already existing from earlier delivery work; it must not introduce a second entry model or reach into entries' data layer.
- Story 6.5's insight overlay is layered onto 6.1's chat state rather than a separate state container, so it cannot be built independently of 6.1's state shape.

1	---
2	title: 'Story 6.2 — Multi-Session Chat History & New Conversation'
3	type: 'feature'
4	created: '2026-11-05'
5	status: 'done'
6	review_loop_iteration: 0
7	baseline_commit: '53de1f87bba2564a87e998b7bb1a515068dd299a'
8	context: ['{project-root}/_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/epic-6-context.md']
9	---
10	
11	<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">
12	
13	## Intent
14	
15	**Problem:** Home/Chat (story 6.1) hard-codes a single auto-bootstrapped session with no way to see past sessions or start a fresh one; `AppDrawer` has no session list at all, just a dead "Novo Chat" button.
16	
17	**Approach:** Add `ChatCubit.switchSession`/`startNewSession` methods that reuse the existing `listSessions()`/`createSession()` repository calls (already backend-correct — no data-layer change needed), carry the session list and a per-session scroll offset on `ChatReady`, and wire `AppDrawer`'s missing "CONVERSAS" section to read/call that same cubit instance via the `BlocProvider<ChatCubit>` already wrapping the drawer's `Scaffold`.
18	
19	## Boundaries & Constraints
20	
21	**Always:**
22	- Drawer reads `context.read<ChatCubit>()`/`BlocBuilder` — the instance `ChatScreen` already provides via `BlocProvider<ChatCubit>.value` (`chat_screen.dart:83-87`); never a second `sl<ChatCubit>()` inside `AppDrawer`.
23	- `switchSession`/`startNewSession` return `Future<Either<Failure, void>>`, `await`ed by their `AppDrawer` tap handlers (closes a gap spec-6-1's review flagged: a cubit action's result must be observed by its caller).
24	- Offline "Novo Chat" leaves the current session untouched; caller shows a transient `SnackBar`, not a dedicated offline banner (Story 6.3's job).
25	- Scroll-offset restore is in-memory only, keyed by `sessionId`, on `ChatCubit` (never Hive) — survives session switches within one app run, resets on restart.
26	- Reuse `_DrawerNavItem`'s tokens (`drawerNavItemPadding`, `textBodyMd`, `textMonoCaption`) — no new design tokens.
27	- An empty `title` renders fallback label "Nova conversa" (contract leaves an untitled session's `title` undocumented).
28	
29	**Ask First:** none identified.
30	
31	**Never:** session rename/delete (no endpoint); paginating past the backend's default first page; Story 6.3's offline composer lock/banner; persisting scroll offset or active-session choice across app restarts.
32	
33	## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix
34	
35	| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
36	|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
37	| Switch session | Drawer open, tap a past session row | `ChatReady` updates to that session's history; scroll jumps to its last recorded offset (or bottom if none) | N/A |
38	| New session online | Tap "Novo Chat" while online | `POST /chat/sessions` succeeds; new empty session becomes active, composer focused, drawer closes | N/A |
39	| New session offline | Tap "Novo Chat" while offline | `createSession()` resolves `Left(Failure.networkOffline)`; current session stays active, drawer closes, `SnackBar` shown | `Failure.networkOffline` surfaced, no crash |
40	| Switch to already-active session | Tap the currently open session's own row | No-op reload; drawer just closes | N/A |
41	
42	</frozen-after-approval>
43	
44	## Code Map
45	
46	- `lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_state.dart:40-69` -- `ChatReady`: add `sessions: List<ChatSession>`, `restoreScrollOffset: double?`; extend `copyWith`.
47	- `lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit.dart:64-114` (`_bootstrap`) -- capture resolved sessions into the emitted `ChatReady`; add `Map<String, double> _scrollOffsets`, `recordScrollOffset`, `switchSession`, `startNewSession` (mirror `_bootstrap`'s match-based error handling, lines 92-113).
48	- `lib/features/chat/domain/repositories/chat_repository.dart:21,31` -- `listSessions()`/`createSession()`, reused as-is.
49	- `lib/core/widgets/app_drawer.dart:17-131` -- wrap body in `BlocBuilder<ChatCubit, ChatState>`; insert a "CONVERSAS" section (mirrors bordered `Container`, lines 78-108) between `_DrawerPrimaryAction` (65-71) and it, shown only when `state is ChatReady`; wire `_DrawerPrimaryAction.onTap` (70) to `startNewSession()`.
50	- `lib/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen.dart:33,59-79` -- on `ChatReady.restoreScrollOffset != null`, `jumpTo` it once instead of `_scrollToBottomSoon()`; add a listener calling `cubit.recordScrollOffset`.
51	- `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml:1071-1155` -- confirms no rename/delete/pagination-required endpoint.
52	- `test/core/navigation/app_router_test.dart:128-156` -- `_FakeChatRepository`, the DI-override pattern to extend.
53	
54	## Tasks & Acceptance
55	
56	**Execution:**
57	- [x] `lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_state.dart` -- add `sessions`/`restoreScrollOffset` to `ChatReady` -- no second state container (AD-12).
58	- [x] `lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit.dart` -- add `switchSession`, `startNewSession`, `recordScrollOffset`; populate `sessions` in `_bootstrap` -- one cubit stays the source of truth.
59	- [x] `lib/core/widgets/app_drawer.dart` -- render CONVERSAS from `ChatReady.sessions`, wire tap → `switchSession`/`startNewSession`, `await` + `SnackBar` on `Left` -- closes the gap at doc-comment lines 8-16.
60	- [x] `lib/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen.dart` -- scroll-offset capture + restore-on-switch -- fulfils the scroll-position AC.
61	- [x] `test/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit_test.dart` -- unit-test `switchSession`/`startNewSession`/offline-create/no-op-on-same-session per the I/O matrix.
62	- [x] `test/core/widgets/app_drawer_test.dart` (pre-existing from Story 1.6, rewritten in place rather than duplicated — its old assertions asserted the now-obsolete "no CONVERSAS section" behavior) -- widget tests: CONVERSAS rendering, tap-to-switch, offline `SnackBar`, mirroring `_FakeChatRepository` (`app_router_test.dart:128-156`).
63	
64	**Acceptance Criteria:**
65	- Given existing Chat Sessions, when I open the side menu, then they're listed under "CONVERSAS" and tapping one switches the active conversation.
66	- Given I tap "Novo Chat", when the new session is created, then it opens empty, composer focused, placeholder "Escreva uma mensagem...".
67	- Given I'm offline, when I tap "Novo Chat", then no session is created, the current conversation is untouched, and I see an error message.
68	- Given I switch back to a session I was previously scrolled up in, when it loads, then it restores that scroll position instead of jumping to the bottom.
69	
70	### Review Findings
71	
72	**Patch:**
73	- [x] [Review][Patch] `ChatCubit.switchSession()`/`startNewSession()` didn't cancel an in-flight `_sendSubscription` or check `_isSending` before switching the active session — a response still streaming into the old session kept mutating whatever session became active next (cross-session message leakage). Fixed via a new `_cancelInFlightSend()`, mirroring `close()`'s own cleanup. [lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit.dart]
74	- [x] [Review][Patch] `_ConversasSection`'s new sort used `DateTime.parse` (not `tryParse`) on `updatedAt` — a malformed timestamp crashed the whole drawer build. ## Intent

**Problem:** Home/Chat (story 6.1) hard-codes a single auto-bootstrapped session with no way to see past sessions or start a fresh one; `AppDrawer` has no session list at all, just a dead "Novo Chat" button.

**Approach:** Add `ChatCubit.switchSession`/`startNewSession` methods that reuse the existing `listSessions()`/`createSession()` repository calls (already backend-correct — no data-layer change needed), carry the session list and a per-session scroll offset on `ChatReady`, and wire `AppDrawer`'s missing "CONVERSAS" section to read/call that same cubit instance via the `BlocProvider<ChatCubit>` already wrapping the drawer's `Scaffold`.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- Drawer reads `context.read<ChatCubit>()`/`BlocBuilder` — the instance `ChatScreen` already provides via `BlocProvider<ChatCubit>.value` (`chat_screen.dart:83-87`); never a second `sl<ChatCubit>()` inside `AppDrawer`.
- `switchSession`/`startNewSession` return `Future<Either<Failure, void>>`, `await`ed by their `AppDrawer` tap handlers (closes a gap spec-6-1's review flagged: a cubit action's result must be observed by its caller).
- Offline "Novo Chat" leaves the current session untouched; caller shows a transient `SnackBar`, not a dedicated offline banner (Story 6.3's job).
- Scroll-offset restore is in-memory only, keyed by `sessionId`, on `ChatCubit` (never Hive) — survives session switches within one app run, resets on restart.
- Reuse `_DrawerNavItem`'s tokens (`drawerNavItemPadding`, `textBodyMd`, `textMonoCaption`) — no new design tokens.
- An empty `title` renders fallback label "Nova conversa" (contract leaves an untitled session's `title` undocumented).

**Ask First:** none identified.

**Never:** session rename/delete (no endpoint); paginating past the backend's default first page; Story 6.3's offline composer lock/banner; persisting scroll offset or active-session choice across app restarts.

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| Switch session | Drawer open, tap a past session row | `ChatReady` updates to that session's history; scroll jumps to its last recorded offset (or bottom if none) | N/A |
| New session online | Tap "Novo Chat" while online | `POST /chat/sessions` succeeds; new empty session becomes active, composer focused, drawer closes | N/A |
| New session offline | Tap "Novo Chat" while offline | `createSession()` resolves `Left(Failure.networkOffline)`; current session stays active, drawer closes, `SnackBar` shown | `Failure.networkOffline` surfaced, no crash |
| Switch to already-active session | Tap the currently open session's own row | No-op reload; drawer just closes | N/A |

</frozen-after-approval>

## Code Map

- `lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_state.dart:40-69` -- `ChatReady`: add `sessions: List<ChatSession>`, `restoreScrollOffset: double?`; extend `copyWith`.
- `lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit.dart:64-114` (`_bootstrap`) -- capture resolved sessions into the emitted `ChatReady`; add `Map<String, double> _scrollOffsets`, `recordScrollOffset`, `switchSession`, `startNewSession` (mirror `_bootstrap`'s match-based error handling, lines 92-113).
- `lib/features/chat/domain/repositories/chat_repository.dart:21,31` -- `listSessions()`/`createSession()`, reused as-is.
- `lib/core/widgets/app_drawer.dart:17-131` -- wrap body in `BlocBuilder<ChatCubit, ChatState>`; insert a "CONVERSAS" section (mirrors bordered `Container`, lines 78-108) between `_DrawerPrimaryAction` (65-71) and it, shown only when `state is ChatReady`; wire `_DrawerPrimaryAction.onTap` (70) to `startNewSession()`.
- `lib/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen.dart:33,59-79` -- on `ChatReady.restoreScrollOffset != null`, `jumpTo` it once instead of `_scrollToBottomSoon()`; add a listener calling `cubit.recordScrollOffset`.
- `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml:1071-1155` -- confirms no rename/delete/pagination-required endpoint.
- `test/core/navigation/app_router_test.dart:128-156` -- `_FakeChatRepository`, the DI-override pattern to extend.

## Tasks & Acceptance

**Execution:**
- [x] `lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_state.dart` -- add `sessions`/`restoreScrollOffset` to `ChatReady` -- no second state container (AD-12).
- [x] `lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit.dart` -- add `switchSession`, `startNewSession`, `recordScrollOffset`; populate `sessions` in `_bootstrap` -- one cubit stays the source of truth.
- [x] `lib/core/widgets/app_drawer.dart` -- render CONVERSAS from `ChatReady.sessions`, wire tap → `switchSession`/`startNewSession`, `await` + `SnackBar` on `Left` -- closes the gap at doc-comment lines 8-16.
- [x] `lib/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen.dart` -- scroll-offset capture + restore-on-switch -- fulfils the scroll-position AC.
- [x] `test/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit_test.dart` -- unit-test `switchSession`/`startNewSession`/offline-create/no-op-on-same-session per the I/O matrix.
- [x] `test/core/widgets/app_drawer_test.dart` (pre-existing from Story 1.6, rewritten in place rather than duplicated — its old assertions asserted the now-obsolete "no CONVERSAS section" behavior) -- widget tests: CONVERSAS rendering, tap-to-switch, offline `SnackBar`, mirroring `_FakeChatRepository` (`app_router_test.dart:128-156`).

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given existing Chat Sessions, when I open the side menu, then they're listed under "CONVERSAS" and tapping one switches the active conversation.
- Given I tap "Novo Chat", when the new session is created, then it opens empty, composer focused, placeholder "Escreva uma mensagem...".
- Given I'm offline, when I tap "Novo Chat", then no session is created, the current conversation is untouched, and I see an error message.

**Dismissed as noise (7):** `_DrawerSessionItem` rows missing a `Key` (cosmetic, no state/animation continuity need in a plain `Column` of stateless rows); the very first bootstrap `ChatReady` being treated as a "new session" by `_lastSessionId`'s null-initial value (working as designed — the code's own doc comment explicitly scopes this to "the initial bootstrap" as one of the triggering events, not an oversight); `switchSession(sessionId)` lacking validation that `sessionId` exists in `current.sessions` (unreachable — the only call site, `_ConversasSection.onSelect`, always passes an id sourced from that same session list); a theoretical concurrent-invocation race on `switchSession`/`startNewSession` (unreachable — `AppDrawer`'s own `_actionTaken` guard plus the drawer staying open throughout the `await` prevent a second call on the same instance, and `Navigator.pop()` only runs after the awaited result resolves); "Novo Chat" tapped during `ChatBootstrapLoading` giving no feedback (already self-disclosed as a known timing-window gap in this story's own `deferred-work.md` entry); a perceived mismatch between this spec's frontmatter `status: 'done'` and `sprint-status.yaml`'s `review` (not a bug — matches `sprint-status.yaml`'s own documented convention: spec status reflects the implementer's own build+self-review completion, external tracking only moves to `done` after this code-review gate, same pattern already used by spec-6-1); the bundled `chat_flow_e2e_test.dart`/`test-summary.md` work being scoped to story 6.1 rather than 6.2 (already self-disclosed — both the commit message and the test-summary's own header name story 6.1 explicitly).

## Spec Change Log

## Design Notes

- `switchSession`/`startNewSession` don't re-emit `ChatBootstrapLoading` (a 4th visible state isn't worth it — "exactly three" governs bubbles, not session-switch chrome). `_scrollOffsets` lives on the long-lived cubit (`chat_injection.dart:50-53`), not `ChatReady`.

## Verification

**Commands:**
- `fvm flutter analyze` -- expected: zero issues
- `fvm flutter test` -- expected: all tests pass, including new cubit/drawer tests

## Suggested Review Order

**Session switching (the new cubit API)**

- Entry point — fetches the target session's history and makes it active; the no-op-on-same-session branch is why "switch to already-active" never re-fetches.
  [`chat_cubit.dart:155`](../../lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit.dart#L155)

- Mirrors `switchSession`, but always runs (no same-session branch) since a new session is never the current one.
  [`chat_cubit.dart:196`](../../lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit.dart#L196)

- Review fix: cancels an in-flight send before switching away, so a still-streaming response can't mutate the session that replaces it.
  [`chat_cubit.dart:407`](../../lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit.dart#L407)

**State shape**

- `ChatReady` gains `sessions` (for the drawer) and `restoreScrollOffset` (for scroll restore) — both set only via direct construction, not `copyWith`.
  [`chat_state.dart:41`](../../lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_state.dart#L41)

- Renders the session list and routes taps to `switchSession`/`startNewSession`, `await`ing the result for a `SnackBar` on failure.
  [`app_drawer.dart:170`](../../lib/core/widgets/app_drawer.dart#L170)

- Same await-and-surface shape for switching.
  [`app_drawer.dart:196`](../../lib/core/widgets/app_drawer.dart#L196)

- The "CONVERSAS" list itself — title + timestamp rows, most-recent-first.
  [`app_drawer.dart:307`](../../lib/core/widgets/app_drawer.dart#L307)

- Review fix: `tryParse` instead of `parse` on `updatedAt`, so a malformed timestamp can't crash the whole drawer build.
  [`app_drawer.dart:333`](../../lib/core/widgets/app_drawer.dart#L333)

**Screen wiring (scroll restore + composer focus)**

- Detects a genuine session change (vs. an in-session update) to decide whether to jump/focus at all.
  [`chat_screen.dart:157`](../../lib/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen.dart#L157)

- Jumps to a session's last recorded scroll offset once its history has attached to the scrollable.
  [`chat_screen.dart:112`](../../lib/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen.dart#L112)

- Requests composer focus when the newly active session has no messages yet (AC2).
  [`chat_screen.dart:129`](../../lib/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen.dart#L129)

- Feeds `ChatCubit.recordScrollOffset` on every scroll update, the data `_jumpToOffset` later reads back.
  [`chat_screen.dart:67`](../../lib/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen.dart#L67)

  [`chat_cubit_test.dart:357`](../../test/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit_test.dart#L357)

  [`app_drawer_test.dart:159`](../../test/core/widgets/app_drawer_test.dart#L159)

  [`chat_screen_test.dart:288`](../../test/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen_test.dart#L288)

**No "biometric-unlock" endpoint — intentional:** the Face ID / Touch ID / PIN barrier of Screen 0.1 is validated entirely on the device, never on the server. The backend only stores the preference (`biometricEnabled`, read and written via `PATCH /account/settings`, section 6.7) — it validates no biometrics. input.description: Read RF04 full requirement text

content.content:
### RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG)
Continuous conversation with the AI agent, with semantic search over previous entries. **Chat messages are conversational and do not create journal entries automatically** — the only exception is the explicit save action described in RF10. Otherwise, the chat queries existing entries via RAG but does not write to them.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Three mandatory UI states: processing/streaming, error, complete response.
- If the response stream drops midway, the partial message stays visible with a failure indication (it does not disappear).

### RF05 — Personal summary export
Generation of a narrative summary by AI (Claude Haiku 4.5) from the user's entries, exportable as PDF, with an additional option to download the raw data without the narrative. No clinical or diagnostic connotation. **Scope: job generation, file download and failure handling — never the quality of the generated narrative text.**

**Acceptance criteria:**
- An export job with zero entries in the period returns a handled error state (not an empty PDF, not a crash).
- A failure generating the narrative text (model timeout) still allows downloading the raw data without the narrative — the export is not blocked by an AI failure.

### RF06 — Semantic search / filter over journal entries
Semantic similarity search (via Voyage AI embeddings, reusing the ones already generated in RF01) combined with metadata filters (date, entry type). There is no filter by tag or category: the backend does not implement it in any endpoint — `GET /entries` and `GET /entries/search` accept only `source` and `dateFrom`/`dateTo`. Tags appear only embedded, read-only, in the `Entry` object (see section 2).

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Searching for a term finds semantically related entries even without the exact word (e.g., searching "ansiedade" returns an entry that only mentions "nervosismo", without the literal term).
- 300 ms search debounce: fast typing triggers a single query, not one per keystroke.
- Results from the local read cache stay consistent with the server after reconnection, without duplicating displayed items *(the architecture is cloud-only; offline allows only viewing already-cached data, not writing)*.
- Two or more filters applied at the same time (`source` + `dateFrom`/`dateTo`) narrow results with AND logic (not OR).
- Clearing the filters returns to the full list without restarting the screen.

### RF07 — Multi-source history (timeline)
A screen whose state depends simultaneously on authentication, synchronization status and entry data.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Session expiration while viewing triggers a new-login prompt without a crash and without losing the scroll position.
- The per-entry synchronization status badge updates independently of the authentication stream.
- No BLoC imports another BLoC directly.

1	import '../../../../core/failure/failure.dart';
2	import '../../domain/entities/chat_message.dart';
3	import '../../domain/entities/chat_session.dart';
4	
5	/// `ChatCubit`'s own sealed state — AD-12: "Chat's state is its own sealed
6	/// class, never forced into `Resource<T>`", because it isn't a single
7	/// fetch (the append-only [ChatReady.messages] list keeps growing one
8	/// token at a time while a response streams in, long after the initial
9	/// bootstrap fetch that produced it has already resolved).
10	sealed class ChatState {
11	  const ChatState();
12	}
13	
14	/// The initial state, and the state while `ChatCubit.init()`'s own
15	/// session-bootstrap (list-or-create-one-session) + history fetch are
16	/// still in flight.
17	class ChatBootstrapLoading extends ChatState {
18	  const ChatBootstrapLoading();
19	}
20	
21	/// I/O matrix: "Bootstrap failure" — `chat-sessions-list`/`create` (or the
22	/// history fetch right after) failed; the screen shows this generic error
23	/// state instead of spinning forever.
24	class ChatBootstrapError extends ChatState {
25	  const ChatBootstrapError(this.failure);
26	
27	  final Failure failure;
28	
29	  @override
30	  bool operator ==(Object other) =>
31	      identical(this, other) ||
32	      (other is ChatBootstrapError && other.failure == failure);
33	
34	  @override
35	  int get hashCode => failure.hashCode;
36	}
37	
38	/// The composer is enabled, [messages] renders — [ChatUiMessage]'s own
39	/// [ChatUiMessage.status] drives each bubble's one of the 3 visible states
40	/// (streaming/failed/complete, RF04's Acceptance Criteria).
41	class ChatReady extends ChatState {
42	  const ChatReady({
43	    required this.sessionId,
44	    required this.messages,
45	    required this.sessions,
46	    this.isSending = false,
47	    this.restoreScrollOffset,
48	  });
49	
50	  final String sessionId;
51	
52	  /// Append-only for the lifetime of this cubit (Code Map) — a message is
53	  /// ever only added to the end, or mutated in place by id (a streaming
54	  /// AI bubble's own `content`/`status`), never removed or reordered.
55	  final List<ChatUiMessage> messages;
56	
57	  /// Every Chat Session the drawer's own "CONVERSAS" section renders
58	  /// (spec-6-2 Code Map) — populated once by `ChatCubit._bootstrap`'s own
59	  /// `listSessions()`/`createSession()` call, then kept current by
60	  /// `ChatCubit.startNewSession` prepending its own result. Never
61	  /// re-fetched/paginated past that first page (Boundaries: "Never:
62	  /// paginating past the backend's default first page").
63	  final List<ChatSession> sessions;
64	
65	  /// Whether `ChatCubit.sendMessage`'s own send is actively in flight —
66	  /// the composer's one enable/disable signal (`_ChatComposer`). Kept as
67	  /// its own field rather than derived by scanning [messages] for a
68	  /// persisted `streaming` status: a message restored from history/cache
69	  /// can legitimately carry that status without a send being in flight
70	  /// (I/O matrix: mid-stream drop), which would otherwise permanently
71	  /// disable the composer.
72	  final bool isSending;
73	
74	  /// The scroll offset `ChatScreen` should jump to the moment this exact
75	  /// [ChatReady] becomes the active session (spec-6-2 I/O matrix: "Switch
76	  /// session") — `ChatCubit._scrollOffsets[sessionId]`'s own last
77	  /// recorded value, or `null` when none was ever recorded (a brand new
78	  /// session, or a session visited for the first time this app run),
79	  /// which `ChatScreen` reads as "jump to bottom instead" (Code Map).
80	  /// Deliberately never cleared by the cubit itself once set — `ChatScreen`
81	  /// only consults it the instant [sessionId] changes from the previous
82	  /// state it observed, so a later unrelated emit (e.g. a streamed token)
83	  /// carrying the same value forward via [copyWith] is harmless (Design
84	  /// Notes).
85	  final double? restoreScrollOffset;
86	
87	  ChatReady copyWith({
88	    List<ChatUiMessage>? messages,
89	    List<ChatSession>? sessions,
90	    bool? isSending,
91	    double? restoreScrollOffset,
92	  }) => ChatReady(
93	    sessionId: sessionId,
94	    messages: messages ?? this.messages,
95	    sessions: sessions ?? this.sessions,
96	    isSending: isSending ?? this.isSending,
97	    restoreScrollOffset: restoreScrollOffset ?? this.restoreScrollOffset,
98	  );
99	}
100	
101	/// One bubble's own presentation-layer shape — distinct from the domain
102	/// `ChatMessage` entity (Code Map) because a message in flight has no
103	/// server-assigned `seq`/`retryCount`/`createdAt` yet; [id] is a locally
104	/// generated, UI-only identifier (`ChatCubit._nextLocalId()`), never the
105	/// server's own message id (Design Notes: `message_created`'s id is the
106	/// *user* message's server id, unused by this story — see
107	/// `ChatStreamEvent`'s own doc).
108	class ChatUiMessage {
109	  const ChatUiMessage({
110	    required this.id,
111	    required this.role,
112	    required this.content,
113	    required this.status,
114	  });
115	
116	  final String id;
117	  final ChatMessageRole role;
118	  final String content;
119	  final ChatMessageStatus status;
120	
121	  ChatUiMessage copyWith({String? content, ChatMessageStatus? status}) =>
122	      ChatUiMessage(
123	        id: id,
124	        role: role,
125	        content: content ?? this.content,
126	        status: status ?? this.status,
127	      );
128	
129	  @override
130	  bool operator ==(Object other) =>
131	      identical(this, other) ||
132	      (other is ChatUiMessage &&
133	          other.id == id &&
134	          other.role == role &&
135	          other.content == content &&
136	          other.status == status);
137	
138	  @override
139	  int get hashCode => Object.hash(id, role, content, status);
140	
141	  @override
142	  String toString() =>
143	      'ChatUiMessage(id: $id, role: $role, content: $content, '
144	      'status: $status)';
145	}

2	
3	import '../../../../core/failure/failure.dart';
4	import '../entities/chat_message.dart';
5	import '../entities/chat_session.dart';
6	import '../entities/chat_stream_event.dart';
7	
8	/// The chat feature's one port — `features/chat/presentation` depends on
9	/// this abstract class only, never `chat/data` (RNF06). Every method but
10	/// [sendMessage] returns `Future<Either<Failure, T>>` (RNF09); [sendMessage]
11	/// alone returns a `Stream` given the SSE nature of its response
12	/// (Boundaries).
13	abstract class ChatRepository {
14	  /// Calls `chat-sessions-list` (`ApiClient.get`, via
15	  /// `ChatRemoteDataSource`) — works offline via the `chat_sessions` Hive
16	  /// box (Code Map): on [Failure.networkOffline]/[Failure.networkTimeout],
17	  /// falls back to a full dump of that box, same "cache fallback"
18	  /// convention `EntriesRepositoryImpl.list()` already uses for its own
19	  /// first/fresh page. Every other [Failure] propagates as `Left`,
20	  /// unmapped (RNF09).
21	  Future<Either<Failure, List<ChatSession>>> listSessions();
22	
23	  /// Calls `chat-sessions-create` (`ApiClient.post`) with no title
24	  /// (Boundaries: "`chat-sessions-create` with no title") — blocked
25	  /// offline per `requirements.md` ("`POST /chat/sessions` — blocked
26	  /// offline"), so unlike [listSessions] there is no cache fallback here:
27	  /// every [Failure], including [Failure.networkOffline], is returned as
28	  /// `Left`, unmapped. On success, persists the new session to the
29	  /// `chat_sessions` Hive box before returning `Right`, same
30	  /// "persist then return" ordering [listSessions] already uses.
31	  Future<Either<Failure, ChatSession>> createSession();
32	
33	  /// Calls `chat-messages-list` (`ApiClient.get`, [sessionId] appended as
34	  /// the one trailing path segment) — works offline via the
35	  /// `chat_messages` Hive box, same cache-fallback convention
36	  /// [listSessions] already uses, filtered to [sessionId] and sorted by
37	  /// `seq` ascending (the backend's own "ordered by seq", `openapi.yaml`).
38	  Future<Either<Failure, List<ChatMessage>>> listMessages(String sessionId);
39	
40	  /// Calls `chat-messages-send` (`ApiClient.postStream`, [sessionId]
41	  /// appended as the one trailing path segment) with `{content}` — the
42	  /// one streaming exception to this port's otherwise all-`Future` shape
43	  /// (Boundaries/RNF09: "every other method returns
44	  /// `Future<Either<Failure, T>>`"). No connectivity resolves immediately
45	  /// to a single `Left(Failure.networkOffline)` emission, never queued
46	  /// (Boundaries) — `ApiClient.postStream`'s own first awaited `Dio.post`
47	  /// call surfaces that failure before any byte streams. A connection that
48	  /// closes without a `done`/`error` SSE event is surfaced as a single
49	  /// trailing `Left(Failure.networkTimeout)` (Design Notes: "the taxonomy
50	  /// has no dedicated 'dropped stream' code"). No local write queue, no
51	  /// Hive persistence of sent messages (Design Notes: chat holds no local
52	  /// write queue for this story).
53	  Stream<Either<Failure, ChatStreamEvent>> sendMessage(
54	    String sessionId,
55	    String content,
56	  );
57	}

7	/// One message bubble — user (Boundaries: `colorChatBubbleUser`, squared
8	/// bottom-right corner) vs AI (`colorSurfaceElevated`, squared bottom-left
9	/// corner, resting [DesignTokens.elevation1]). Exactly the 3 visible
10	/// states RF04's Acceptance Criteria names render here, driven by
11	/// [ChatUiMessage.status]: `streaming` (progressive text + blinking
12	/// cursor), `failed` (a generic error indicator replaces the timestamp
13	/// slot — never the tap-to-retry copy, Boundaries: "generic error
14	/// indicator (not retry copy)" — Story 6.3's job), `complete` (plain
15	/// text, nothing else). [ChatUiMessage.content] itself is rendered as-is
16	/// in every state — never cleared on failure (I/O matrix).
17	class ChatBubble extends StatefulWidget {
18	  const ChatBubble({required this.message, super.key});
19	
20	  final ChatUiMessage message;
21	
22	  @override
23	  State<ChatBubble> createState() => _ChatBubbleState();
24	}
25	
26	class _ChatBubbleState extends State<ChatBubble>
27	    with SingleTickerProviderStateMixin {
28	  late final AnimationController _cursorController;
29	
30	  @override
31	  void initState() {
32	    super.initState();
33	    _cursorController = AnimationController(
34	      vsync: this,
35	      duration: const Duration(milliseconds: 600),
36	    );
37	    _syncCursorAnimation();
38	  }
39	
40	  @override
41	  void didUpdateWidget(ChatBubble oldWidget) {
42	    super.didUpdateWidget(oldWidget);
43	    _syncCursorAnimation();
44	  }
45	
46	  /// Keeps the ticker running only while actually needed — a message
47	  /// that finalizes to `complete`/`failed` must stop ticking forever
48	  /// after, both so a long-lived chat session never leaks one live
49	  /// `AnimationController` per past message, and so nothing waiting on
50	  /// "every animation in the tree has settled" (e.g. a test's own
51	  /// `pumpAndSettle()`) ever blocks on a bubble that finished streaming.
52	  void _syncCursorAnimation() {
53	    final shouldAnimate = widget.message.status == ChatMessageStatus.streaming;
54	    if (shouldAnimate && !_cursorController.isAnimating) {
55	      _cursorController.repeat(reverse: true);
56	    } else if (!shouldAnimate && _cursorController.isAnimating) {
57	      _cursorController.stop();
58	    }
59	  }
60	
61	  @override
62	  void dispose() {
63	    _cursorController.dispose();
64	    super.dispose();
65	  }
66	
67	  @override
68	  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
69	    final message = widget.message;
70	    final isUser = message.role == ChatMessageRole.user;
71	    // Boundaries: "cursor skipped under
72	    // `MediaQuery.of(context).disableAnimations`" — the real token text
73	    // itself always reveals as real tokens actually arrive (there is no
74	    // separate typing-speed animation to collapse here), only the
75	    // blinking-cursor glyph is conditional on Reduce Motion.
76	    final reduceMotion = MediaQuery.of(context).disableAnimations;
77	    final showCursor =
78	        message.status == ChatMessageStatus.streaming && !reduceMotion;
79	
80	    return Align(
81	      alignment: isUser ? Alignment.centerRight : Alignment.centerLeft,
82	      child: Container(
83	        margin: const EdgeInsets.only(bottom: DesignTokens.chatBubbleGap),
84	        constraints: BoxConstraints(
85	          maxWidth:
86	              MediaQuery.of(context).size.width *
87	              DesignTokens.chatBubbleMaxWidthFraction,
88	        ),
89	        padding: DesignTokens.chatBubblePadding,
90	        decoration: BoxDecoration(
91	          color: isUser
92	              ? DesignTokens.colorChatBubbleUser
93	              : DesignTokens.colorSurfaceElevated,
94	          borderRadius: BorderRadius.only(
95	            topLeft: const Radius.circular(DesignTokens.radiusMd),
96	            topRight: const Radius.circular(DesignTokens.radiusMd),
97	            bottomLeft: Radius.circular(isUser ? DesignTokens.radiusMd : 0),
98	            bottomRight: Radius.circular(isUser ? 0 : DesignTokens.radiusMd),
99	          ),
100	          boxShadow: isUser ? null : DesignTokens.elevation1,
101	        ),
102	        child: Column(
103	          crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
104	          mainAxisSize: MainAxisSize.min,
105	          children: [
106	            Text.rich(
107	              TextSpan(
108	                children: [
109	                  TextSpan(text: message.content),
110	                  if (showCursor)
111	                    WidgetSpan(
112	                      alignment: PlaceholderAlignment.middle,
113	                      child: ExcludeSemantics(
114	                        child: FadeTransition(
115	                          opacity: _cursorController,
116	                          child: const Text('▏'),
117	                        ),
118	                      ),
119	                    ),
120	                ],
121	              ),
122	              style: DesignTokens.textBodyLg.copyWith(
123	                color: DesignTokens.colorTextPrimary,
124	              ),
125	            ),
126	            if (message.status == ChatMessageStatus.failed) ...[
127	              const SizedBox(height: DesignTokens.spacingXs),
128	              Container(
129	                padding: DesignTokens.chatFailureIndicatorPadding,
130	                decoration: const BoxDecoration(
131	                  color: DesignTokens.colorErrorBg,
132	                  borderRadius: BorderRadius.all(
133	                    Radius.circular(DesignTokens.radiusSm),
134	                  ),
135	                ),
136	                child: Text(
137	                  'Falha ao gerar resposta',
138	                  style: DesignTokens.textCaptionSm.copyWith(
139	                    color: DesignTokens.colorError,
140	                  ),
141	                ),
142	              ),
143	            ],
144	          ],
145	        ),
146	      ),
147	    );
148	  }
149	}

4	import '../../domain/entities/sync_badge_state.dart';
5	
6	/// `EntryRecordCard`'s own sync badge (Code Map) — a colored dot
7	/// ([DesignTokens.colorWarningSync]/[DesignTokens.colorSuccess]/
8	/// [DesignTokens.colorError]) plus its text label, always visible (not
9	/// hidden behind a tap). "Accessible label on tap/long-focus" is split
10	/// across two single-purpose widgets rather than two that both also
11	/// announce it: the dot's [Tooltip] (`excludeFromSemantics: true`) gives
12	/// the *visual* long-press popup only, while the one [Semantics] node
13	/// wrapping the whole badge (below) is the single accessibility
14	/// announcement on focus — code-review round 1 finding: a [Tooltip] left
15	/// at its default `excludeFromSemantics: false` injects its own semantics
16	/// label too, so pairing it with an outer [Semantics] of the same label
17	/// double-announced it to screen readers.
18	///
19	/// Only an [SyncBadgeError] badge is ever tappable (Boundaries): a
20	/// [Failure.retryable] one calls [onRetryTap] on tap (I/O matrix: "Tap
21	/// calls `tracker.retry(tempId)`, re-sends same payload"); a
22	/// non-retryable one instead toggles an inline explanation
23	/// ([SyncBadgeError.failure]'s own `message`) with no network call and no
24	/// retry affordance (Boundaries: "else render inline explanation text, no
25	/// tap affordance"). [SyncBadgeSynchronizing]/[SyncBadgeSynchronized] are
26	/// never tappable at all.
27	class SyncBadge extends StatefulWidget {
28	  const SyncBadge({
29	    required this.state,
30	    this.onRetryTap,
31	    this.compact = false,
32	    super.key,
33	  });
34	
35	  final SyncBadgeState state;
36	
37	  /// Called on tap only for a retryable [SyncBadgeError] — ignored (never
38	  /// even referenced) for every other state, and for a non-retryable
39	  /// error (Boundaries: "no tap affordance" there means no retry action,
40	  /// not no tap at all — tapping a non-retryable error still reveals its
41	  /// explanation, just never calls this).
42	  final VoidCallback? onRetryTap;
43	
44	  /// `EntryRecordCard`'s own variant (correction) — `cerne-prototype.html`'s
45	  /// Tela 4 record card renders the label lowercase in plain
46	  /// `colorTextSecondary`, next to the colored dot, not the state's own
47	  /// color; `EntryDetailScreen` (no prototype ground truth for that
48	  /// screen) keeps the default colored/capitalized rendering, so this is
49	  /// opt-in rather than this widget's new default.
50	  final bool compact;
51	
52	  @override
53	  State<SyncBadge> createState() => _SyncBadgeState();
54	}
55	
56	class _SyncBadgeState extends State<SyncBadge> {
57	  bool _explanationExpanded = false;
58	
59	  @override
60	  void didUpdateWidget(SyncBadge oldWidget) {
61	    super.didUpdateWidget(oldWidget);
62	    // A retry attempt (or any other state transition) collapses a
63	    // previously-shown explanation — stale text from a superseded
64	    // failure should never linger once the badge has moved on (e.g.
65	    // synchronizing -> a *new* error after a retry that fails again).
66	    if (widget.state != oldWidget.state) {
67	      _explanationExpanded = false;
68	    }
69	  }
70	
71	  @override
72	  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
73	    final state = widget.state;
74	    final (color, label) = switch (state) {
75	      SyncBadgeSynchronizing() => (
76	        DesignTokens.colorWarningSync,
77	        'Sincronizando',
78	      ),
79	      SyncBadgeSynchronized() => (DesignTokens.colorSuccess, 'Sincronizado'),
80	      SyncBadgeError() => (DesignTokens.colorError, 'Erro de sincronização'),
81	    };
82	
83	    // Reuses the existing kanban color-dot token (8dp) rather than a new
84	    // literal (RNF08) — same shape/role (a small colored status dot), just
85	    // a different screen. `excludeFromSemantics: true` (Review finding):
86	    // the outer `Semantics(label: label)` below is this badge's one and
87	    // only accessibility announcement — this Tooltip exists purely for
88	    // its own visual long-press popup.
89	    final dot = Tooltip(
90	      message: label,
91	      excludeFromSemantics: true,
92	      child: Container(
93	        width: DesignTokens.kanbanDotSize,
94	        height: DesignTokens.kanbanDotSize,
95	        decoration: BoxDecoration(color: color, shape: BoxShape.circle),
96	      ),
97	    );
98	
99	    // [compact]: lowercase text in `colorTextSecondary` instead of the
100	    // state's own color — the dot alone still carries that color. Only
101	    // the *visible* text changes; [label] itself (the accessible string
102	    // below) stays capitalized either way.
103	    final displayLabel = widget.compact ? label.toLowerCase() : label;
104	    final textColor = widget.compact ? DesignTokens.colorTextSecondary : color;
105	
106	    // `ExcludeSemantics` (Review finding): without it, the visible `Text`
107	    // below contributes its *own* implicit semantics label ("Sincronizando",
108	    // same string) that merges straight into the explicit `Semantics(label:
109	    // label)` container wrapping this whole row — doubling the announced
110	    // label even after the dot's own `Tooltip` was already excluded above.
111	    // The one `Semantics(label: label)` node is this badge's single source
112	    // of truth for its accessible text; this row is purely visual.
113	    final labelRow = ExcludeSemantics(
114	      child: Row(
115	        mainAxisSize: MainAxisSize.min,
116	        children: [
117	          dot,
118	          const SizedBox(width: DesignTokens.spacingXs),
119	          Text(
120	            displayLabel,
121	            style: DesignTokens.textMonoCaption.copyWith(color: textColor),
122	          ),
123	        ],
124	      ),
125	    );
126	
127	    if (state is! SyncBadgeError) {
128	      // `container: true` (Review finding) — without it, a `Semantics`
129	      // widget with no interactive descendant doesn't form its own node;
130	      // Flutter merges its `label` up into the nearest explicit container
131	      // ancestor instead (e.g. the Scaffold's own), so `label` alone is
132	      // never exactly what a screen reader (or `find.bySemanticsLabel`)
133	      // reports for this widget specifically.
134	      return Semantics(label: label, container: true, child: labelRow);
135	    }
136	
137	    final retryable = state.failure.retryable;
138	    return Semantics(
139	      label: label,
140	      container: true,
141	      button: true,
142	      child: InkWell(
143	        onTap: () {
144	          if (retryable) {
145	            widget.onRetryTap?.call();
146	          } else {
147	            setState(() => _explanationExpanded = !_explanationExpanded);
148	          }
149	        },
150	        child: ConstrainedBox(
151	          constraints: const BoxConstraints(
152	            minWidth: DesignTokens.insertionModalTapTargetMin,
153	            minHeight: DesignTokens.insertionModalTapTargetMin,
154	          ),
155	          child: Align(
156	            alignment: Alignment.centerLeft,
157	            child: Column(
158	              crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
159	              mainAxisSize: MainAxisSize.min,
160	              children: [
161	                labelRow,
162	                if (!retryable && _explanationExpanded)
163	                  Padding(
164	                    padding: const EdgeInsets.only(top: DesignTokens.spacingXs),
165	                    child: Text(
166	                      state.failure.message,
167	                      style: DesignTokens.textCaptionSm.copyWith(
168	                        color: DesignTokens.colorTextSecondary,
169	                      ),
170	                    ),
171	                  ),
172	              ],
173	            ),
174	          ),
175	        ),
176	      ),
177	    );
178	  }
179	}

184	
185	- **Expired session:** an overlay on the chat that keeps history and scroll position — the expired token must not discard the conversation state in memory before re-authentication. Re-authenticating goes back to the Biometria screen, not to a full form.
186	- **Offline:** blocks **sending new messages** (send icon disabled, explanatory banner), but **history stays visible and navigable**. The prototype does not show what happens to the insertion modal (text/audio/photo) when offline.
187	- **Asynchronous processing — audio transcription:** a loading state (spinner + frozen waveform) and two outcomes (success/error); the error always offers "Tentar novamente" and never loses the recorded audio.
188	- **Asynchronous processing — photo OCR:** same pattern as audio, with one extra exit on error: "Salvar só a foto", which saves the record even without extracted text.
189	- **Asynchronous processing — export:** two loading stages (preparing → generating the AI summary) before the result; on error, the raw data is always available for download — the failure is isolated to the AI narrative, never to the user's data.
190	- **Dashboard narrative unavailable:** the chart loads normally but the AI summary paragraph fails — distinct from "zero entries" (lack of data) and needs its own error message.
191

195	
196	1. **"29 frames" vs. "32 states":** the prototype has 32 distinct navigable states, but the number of frames (29) suggests that some state families should be one screen with internal state, not separate routes (e.g., a single `ExportSheet` with a status enum instead of 5 routes). Consider this when designing navigation.
197	2. **Account deletion without a success screen:** both "Sair" and "Apagar tudo" return to the Biometria screen; there is no "account deleted" or "you signed out" screen.
198	3. **Login vs. sign-up:** the same screen toggled by a text link; the prototype shows no extra sign-up fields (e.g., password confirmation, name). Whether sign-up needs extra fields is a product decision not covered visually.
199	4. **Insertion modal when offline:** not represented.
200	5. **Switching tabs in the insertion modal:** opening the modal always resets every tab to `idle`/empty, but switching tabs *during* a modal session is not cleared automatically — the expected behavior (e.g., whether an ongoing recording is discarded on tab switch) is not defined by the prototype.

6	/// AD-4 — the one place retry policy lives. Retries only the 6 server
7	/// `retryable:true` codes (`error-taxonomy.md`); every other failure
8	/// (including the local `MalformedResponse`) surfaces once, unretried.
9	///
10	/// Design note (docs/input is silent on the schedule): fixed 500ms delay,
11	/// max 2 retries.
12	class RetryInterceptor extends Interceptor {
13	  RetryInterceptor(this._dio);
14	
15	  final Dio _dio;
16	
17	  /// The 6 server `retryable:true` codes — the only codes this interceptor
18	  /// ever retries.
19	  static const Set<String> retryableCodes = {
20	    'NETWORK_TIMEOUT',
21	    'NETWORK_OFFLINE',
22	    'PII_CHECK_FAILED',
23	    'EMBEDDING_FAILED',
24	    'AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT',
25	    'RATE_LIMITED',
26	  };
27	
28	  /// Non-idempotent POSTs with no client-supplied idempotency key — a
29	  /// transparent retry here would silently resend the identical request
30	  /// (the same chat message content, or a second session-create) rather
31	  /// than surfacing the failure once to the caller. `dioErrorCodeOf` can
32	  /// return a retryable code for these from `DioException.type` alone
33	  /// (`NETWORK_TIMEOUT`/`NETWORK_OFFLINE`) even before any response body
34	  /// exists to carry the real `{code,message}`, so excluding by function
35	  /// name here is the only place this can be enforced.
36	  static const Set<String> neverRetriedFunctions = {
37	    'chat-messages-send',
38	    'chat-sessions-create',
39	  };
40	
41	  static const int maxRetries = 2;
42	  static const Duration retryDelay = Duration(milliseconds: 500);
43	
44	  static const _attemptKey = 'cerne_retry_attempt';

---
title: 'Story 6.3 — Dropped-Stream Resilience & Offline Composer Lock'
type: 'feature'
created: '2026-11-05'
status: 'draft'
review_loop_iteration: 0
context: ['{project-root}/_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/epic-6-context.md']
---

<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">

## Intent

**Problem:** A dropped/failed AI response is marked `failed` with no way to retry it — `ChatCubit` has no retry method at all. The composer has no offline-awareness either; `_ChatComposer`'s own doc comment (`chat_screen.dart:284-288`) names this exact gap as "Story 6.3's job," and there is no device-connectivity detection anywhere in the app yet.

**Approach:** Add `ChatCubit.retryMessage`, calling a new `ChatRepository.retryMessage`/`ChatRemoteDataSource.retryMessage` pair that mirrors `sendMessage`'s SSE consumption against `chat-messages-retry`. Introduce a feature-local `ConnectivityWatcher` (domain service, `connectivity_plus`-backed impl) that `ChatCubit` consumes to drive a new `ChatReady.isOffline` flag, which gates the composer, a new offline banner, and the drawer's "Novo Chat".

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- Tap-to-retry renders only on a `failed` AI bubble, never a user message — exact prototype copy "Falha ao gerar resposta — toque para tentar novamente" (`cerne-prototype.html`), replacing `chat_bubble.dart:136-141`'s static text; tappable, 44pt min target (`DesignTokens.insertionModalTapTargetMin`, reused cross-feature already by `sync_badge.dart:150-154`), `Semantics(button: true)`.
- Retry resets the *same* bubble (id, position) to `streaming`/empty content, then reuses `ChatCubit._applyStreamEvent`/`_markFailed` (`chat_cubit.dart:358-421`) unchanged — never appends a second AI bubble, never re-sends a duplicate question.
- Retry is keyed by the original user message's persisted id, captured from the `message_created` event this story starts consuming (currently a no-op, `chat_cubit.dart:366-371`). Add `ChatUiMessage.serverId`: set from `_fromDomain` (`chat_cubit.dart:251-256`, historical messages already carry it as `message.id`) and, for an in-session optimistic send, from `message_created`'s `userMessageId`.
- `ConnectivityWatcher` is a feature-local domain service (`chat/domain/services/`) with a `connectivity_plus`-backed impl (`chat/data/services/`), injected straight into `ChatCubit`'s constructor — mirrors `MicRecorder`'s domain/data split (`lib/features/capture/domain/services/mic_recorder.dart`), never routed through `ChatRepository` (connectivity isn't fetched/cached domain data, and `AudioEntryCubit` already injects a core-ish service directly, same precedent).
- `ChatReady` gains `isOffline` (bool, default `false`). Drives: `_ChatComposer.canSend` (text field + send icon only — the "+" stays tappable per its own doc, `chat_screen.dart:284-288`); a new banner between `_ChatHeader` and the message list (`chat_screen.dart:148-150`) with exact copy "Sem conexão — histórico disponível, novas mensagens bloqueadas", `Icons.wifi_off`, `DesignTokens.colorInfoOffline`/`colorOnPrimary` (both tokens already exist, no new token needed); and `AppDrawer`'s "Novo Chat" (`app_drawer.dart:73-77`, disabled + dimmed when offline).
- Add `'chat-messages-retry'` to `RetryInterceptor.neverRetriedFunctions` (`retry_interceptor.dart:36-39`) — same non-idempotent-POST rationale already applied to `chat-messages-send`.

**Ask First:** none identified.

**Never:**

- Retry is keyed by the user message's persisted id, captured from `message_created` (currently a no-op, `chat_cubit.dart:366-371`). Add `ChatUiMessage.serverId`: from `_fromDomain` (`chat_cubit.dart:251-256`, `= message.id`) and, for an in-session send, from `message_created`'s `userMessageId`.
- `ConnectivityWatcher`: feature-local domain service (`chat/domain/services/`) + `connectivity_plus` impl (`chat/data/services/`), injected into `ChatCubit`'s ctor — mirrors `MicRecorder`'s domain/data split (`lib/features/capture/domain/services/mic_recorder.dart`), never through `ChatRepository`.
- `ChatReady` gains `isOffline` (default `false`), driving: `_ChatComposer.canSend` (`chat_screen.dart:304`, text+send only — "+" stays tappable); an offline banner between `_ChatHeader` and the list (`chat_screen.dart:148-150`), copy "Sem conexão — histórico disponível, novas mensagens bloqueadas", `Icons.wifi_off`, `DesignTokens.colorInfoOffline`/`colorOnPrimary` (existing tokens); `AppDrawer`'s "Novo Chat" (`app_drawer.dart:73-77`, disabled + dimmed).
- Add `'chat-messages-retry'` to `RetryInterceptor.neverRetriedFunctions` (`retry_interceptor.dart:36-39`).

**Ask First:** none identified.

**Never:**
- Changing `ChatRepositoryImpl`'s existing reactive `Failure.networkOffline` handling — `isOffline` is additive only.
- Calling `chat-messages-retry` with no `serverId` (stream dropped before `message_created`) — falls back to a full `sendMessage` resend of the same content into the same bubble slot.
- A second retry while one is in flight — reuses `_isSending` verbatim.
- Disabling the "+" when offline, or removing `AppDrawer._startNewSession`'s offline `SnackBar` (spec-6-2) — both stay.

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| Tap retry, normal | Failed AI bubble; preceding user message has `serverId` | Bubble resets to `streaming`/empty, fills via `chat-messages-retry`'s SSE, ends `complete` | A second failure re-marks `failed`, stays tappable |
| Tap retry, no `serverId` | Stream dropped before `message_created` arrived | Falls back to `sendMessage`, same content, same slot | Same handling as any send |
| Goes offline mid-session | `ConnectivityWatcher` emits `false` | Composer + "Novo Chat" disable, banner appears, history stays scrollable | N/A |
| Comes back online | `ConnectivityWatcher` emits `true` | Banner disappears, composer + "Novo Chat" re-enable | N/A |

</frozen-after-approval>
