- `lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit.dart:18` (ctor) -- add `ConnectivityWatcher` param; subscribe, store `_isOffline`, emit on `ChatReady` when it changes.
- `lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit.dart:313-317` (`sendMessage` `onData`) -- on `ChatMessageCreatedEvent`, set `userMessage.serverId` before `_applyStreamEvent`.
- `lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit.dart:251-256` (`_fromDomain`) -- `serverId: message.id`.
- `lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit.dart:274-341` (`sendMessage`) -- mirror for new `retryMessage(aiMessageId)`: same guards, find target + preceding user message's `serverId`, reset content/status, subscribe (`retryMessage` or `sendMessage` fallback), reuse `_applyStreamEvent`/`_markFailed`/`_finishSending`.
- `lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_state.dart:41-98` (`ChatReady`) -- add `isOffline` + `copyWith`.
- `lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_state.dart:108-144` (`ChatUiMessage`) -- add `serverId` + `copyWith`/`==`/`hashCode`/`toString`.
- `lib/features/chat/domain/repositories/chat_repository.dart:53-56` -- add `retryMessage(sessionId, userMessageId)`.
- `lib/features/chat/data/repositories/chat_repository_impl.dart:116-122` (`sendMessage`) -- sibling `retryMessage` passthrough.
- `lib/features/chat/data/datasources/chat_remote_data_source.dart:137-271` -- extract shared SSE buffer/parse helper; add `retryMessage` hitting `chat-messages-retry`, `pathParams: [sessionId, userMessageId]`, `data: const {}`.
- `lib/features/chat/domain/services/connectivity_watcher.dart` (new) -- `abstract class ConnectivityWatcher { Stream<bool> watch(); }`, mirrors `mic_recorder.dart`.
- `lib/features/chat/data/services/connectivity_plus_watcher.dart` (new) -- `connectivity_plus` impl.
- `lib/features/chat/chat_injection.dart:32-53` -- register `ConnectivityWatcher`; inject into `ChatCubit` (line 50-51).
- `lib/core/network/retry_interceptor.dart:36-39` -- add `'chat-messages-retry'`.
- `lib/features/chat/presentation/widgets/chat_bubble.dart:17-24,126-143` -- add `onRetry` callback; tappable region, min 44pt, `Semantics(button: true)`.
- `lib/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen.dart:181-189` -- wire `onRetry: () => cubit.retryMessage(messages[index].id)`.
- `lib/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen.dart:148-150` -- insert offline banner (`state is ChatReady && state.isOffline`).
- `lib/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen.dart:304` -- `canSend` += `!state.isOffline`.
- `lib/core/widgets/app_drawer.dart:73-77` -- gate "Novo Chat" on `!isOffline` via `BlocBuilder`.
- `pubspec.yaml` -- add via `fvm flutter pub add connectivity_plus`.
- `test/features/chat/**`, `test/core/widgets/app_drawer_test.dart` -- extend per the I/O matrix; reuse `test/core/navigation/app_router_test.dart:128-156`'s `_FakeChatRepository`; add a fake `ConnectivityWatcher`.

## Tasks & Acceptance

**Execution:**
- [ ] `chat/domain/services/connectivity_watcher.dart`, `chat/data/services/connectivity_plus_watcher.dart` -- create the abstraction + impl.
- [ ] `chat/presentation/cubit/chat_state.dart` -- `ChatReady.isOffline`, `ChatUiMessage.serverId`.
- [ ] `chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit.dart` -- connectivity subscription, `serverId` capture, `retryMessage`.
- [ ] `chat/domain/repositories/chat_repository.dart`, `data/repositories/chat_repository_impl.dart`, `data/datasources/chat_remote_data_source.dart` -- `retryMessage` through all three layers.
- [ ] `chat/chat_injection.dart` -- wire `ConnectivityWatcher` into DI and `ChatCubit`.
- [ ] `core/network/retry_interceptor.dart` -- exclude `chat-messages-retry` from transparent retry.
- [ ] `chat/presentation/widgets/chat_bubble.dart`, `presentation/screens/chat_screen.dart`, `core/widgets/app_drawer.dart` -- tap-to-retry UI, offline banner, composer lock, "Novo Chat" disable.
- [ ] Extend the test files listed in the Code Map per the I/O matrix.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given a dropped/failed AI response, when I tap its retry copy, then the same bubble regenerates in place, with no new question bubble and no re-send of the question.
- Given I'm offline, when Home/Chat is open, then the composer is disabled with the offline banner visible, while history stays fully visible and scrollable.
- Given I'm offline, when I open the side menu, then "Novo Chat" is disabled.
- Given connectivity returns, when `isOffline` flips back, then the composer and "Novo Chat" re-enable automatically.

## Design Notes

- `serverId` (not reusing `id`) avoids ever swapping a `ChatUiMessage.id` mid-stream — `id` stays the stable lookup key; `serverId` is only the value sent to `chat-messages-retry`.
- `ConnectivityWatcher` lives in `chat/domain/services/`, not `core/`, since no other feature needs connectivity yet; promote it later if one does.

# Sync Sprint Status

Shared sub-step for updating `sprint-status.yaml` during build. Called from any route (plan-code-review, one-shot, future routes) with a `target_status` parameter.

## Preconditions

Skip this entire file (return to caller) if ANY of:
- `story_key` is unset
- `/Users/wagnerduarte/Documents/Faculdade/2026.2/TCC/cerne-ciclo-b/_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/sprint-status.yaml` does not exist on disk

## Instructions

1. Load the FULL `/Users/wagnerduarte/Documents/Faculdade/2026.2/TCC/cerne-ciclo-b/_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/sprint-status.yaml` file.
2. Find the `development_status` entry matching `{story_key}`. If not found, warn the user once (`"{story_key} not found in sprint-status; skipping sprint sync"`) and return to caller.
3. **Idempotency check.** If `development_status[{story_key}]` is already at `target_status` or a later state (`review` is later than `in-progress`; `done` is later than both), return to caller — no write needed. Never regress a story's status.
4. Set `development_status[{story_key}]` to `{target_status}`.
5. **Epic lift (only when `target_status` = `in-progress`).** Derive the parent epic key as `epic-{N}` from the leading numeric segment of `{story_key}` (e.g., `3-2-digest-delivery` → `epic-3`). If that entry exists and is `backlog`, set it to `in-progress`. Leave it alone otherwise. Skip this sub-step entirely when `target_status` is not `in-progress`.
6. Refresh `last_updated` to the current date.
7. Save the file, preserving ALL comments and structure including STATUS DEFINITIONS and WORKFLOW NOTES.

Fixed by constructing the cubit/watcher pair inside the test body itself for the two offline-gating tests (documented inline in the test file).

  `pubspec.yaml`/`pubspec.lock` updated via `fvm flutter pub add connectivity_plus` (now `connectivity_plus: ^7.3.2`); resolves with no conflicts.
  
  Marked the spec's own Tasks checklist as complete; left `status: in-progress` untouched since that's owned by the review-loop step, not this implementation pass.
  
  ## Risks / left incomplete
  - Nothing from the spec is incomplete — all boundaries, the I/O matrix, and all four acceptance criteria are implemented and covered by tests.
  - Minor design judgment call: `ConnectivityWatcher.watch()` emits an initial "current status" snapshot (via `checkConnectivity()`) in addition to future changes, which the spec's abstract Code Map signature didn't explicitly require — done for correctness (so a cold start while already offline is reflected immediately) and documented as best-effort/non-contractual in the port's own doc comment; it's covered by a dedicated unit test and doesn't affect any acceptance criterion (all of which only exercise the mid-session transition).
  - No device/simulator/CI exists yet (per AGENTS.md), so the real `connectivity_plus` platform channels are never exercised for real — only faked in the two real-DI test files, mirroring the existing `record`/`flutter_secure_storage` convention.

title: 'Story 6.3 — Dropped-Stream Resilience & Offline Composer Lock'
type: 'feature'
created: '2026-11-05'
status: 'in-progress'
review_loop_iteration: 0
baseline_commit: '43351cf59fa0a85125a5d50eefbe984600c7b403'
context: ['{project-root}/_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/epic-6-context.md']

<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">

## Intent

**Problem:** A dropped/failed AI response is marked `failed` with no retry path — `ChatCubit` has none. The composer has no offline-awareness either; `_ChatComposer`'s own doc (`chat_screen.dart:284-288`) names this gap as "Story 6.3's job," and no connectivity detection exists anywhere in the app.

**Approach:** Add `ChatCubit.retryMessage`, backed by a new `ChatRepository.retryMessage`/`ChatRemoteDataSource.retryMessage` mirroring `sendMessage`'s SSE consumption against `chat-messages-retry`. Add a feature-local `ConnectivityWatcher` (domain service, `connectivity_plus` impl) that `ChatCubit` consumes into a new `ChatReady.isOffline` flag, gating the composer, a new offline banner, and the drawer's "Novo Chat".

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- Tap-to-retry renders only on a `failed` AI bubble — copy "Falha ao gerar resposta — toque para tentar novamente" (`cerne-prototype.html`), replacing `chat_bubble.dart:136-141`; tappable, 44pt min (`DesignTokens.insertionModalTapTargetMin`), `Semantics(button: true)`.
- Retry resets the *same* bubble (id, position) to `streaming`/empty, then reuses `_applyStreamEvent`/`_markFailed` (`chat_cubit.dart:358-421`) unchanged — never a second bubble, never a duplicate question.
- Retry is keyed by the user message's persisted id, captured from `message_created` (currently a no-op, `chat_cubit.dart:366-371`). Add `ChatUiMessage.serverId`: from `_fromDomain` (`chat_cubit.dart:251-256`, `= message.id`) and, for an in-session send, from `message_created`'s `userMessageId`.
- `ConnectivityWatcher`: feature-local domain service (`chat/domain/services/`) + `connectivity_plus` impl (`chat/data/services/`), injected into `ChatCubit`'s ctor — mirrors `MicRecorder`'s domain/data split (`lib/features/capture/domain/services/mic_recorder.dart`), never through `ChatRepository`.
- `ChatReady` gains `isOffline` (default `false`), driving: `_ChatComposer.canSend` (`chat_screen.dart:304`, text+send only — "+" stays tappable); an offline banner between `_ChatHeader` and the list (`chat_screen.dart:148-150`), copy "Sem conexão — histórico disponível, novas mensagens bloqueadas", `Icons.wifi_off`, `DesignTokens.colorInfoOffline`/`colorOnPrimary` (existing tokens); `AppDrawer`'s "Novo Chat" (`app_drawer.dart:73-77`, disabled + dimmed).
- Add `'chat-messages-retry'` to `RetryInterceptor.neverRetriedFunctions` (`retry_interceptor.dart:36-39`).

**Ask First:** none identified.

**Never:**
- Changing `ChatRepositoryImpl`'s existing reactive `Failure.networkOffline` handling — `isOffline` is additive only.
- Calling `chat-messages-retry` with no `serverId` (stream dropped before `message_created`) — falls back to a full `sendMessage` resend of the same content into the same bubble slot.
- A second retry while one is in flight — reuses `_isSending` verbatim.
- Disabling the "+" when offline, or removing `AppDrawer._startNewSession`'s offline `SnackBar` (spec-6-2) — both stay.

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| Tap retry, normal | Failed AI bubble; preceding user message has `serverId` | Bubble resets to `streaming`/empty, fills via `chat-messages-retry`'s SSE, ends `complete` | A second failure re-marks `failed`, stays tappable |
| Tap retry, no `serverId` | Stream dropped before `message_created` arrived | Falls back to `sendMessage`, same content, same slot | Same handling as any send |
| Goes offline mid-session | `ConnectivityWatcher` emits `false` | Composer + "Novo Chat" disable, banner appears, history stays scrollable | N/A |
| Comes back online | `ConnectivityWatcher` emits `true` | Banner disappears, composer + "Novo Chat" re-enable | N/A |

</frozen-after-approval>

## Code Map

- `lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit.dart:18` (ctor) -- add `ConnectivityWatcher` param; subscribe, store `_isOffline`, emit on `ChatReady` when it changes.
- `lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit.dart:313-317` (`sendMessage` `onData`) -- on `ChatMessageCreatedEvent`, set `userMessage.serverId` before `_applyStreamEvent`.
- `lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit.dart:251-256` (`_fromDomain`) -- `serverId: message.id`.
- `lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit.dart:274-341` (`sendMessage`) -- mirror for new `retryMessage(aiMessageId)`: same guards, find target + preceding user message's `serverId`, reset content/status, subscribe (`retryMessage` or `sendMessage` fallback), reuse `_applyStreamEvent`/`_markFailed`/`_finishSending`.
- `lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_state.dart:41-98` (`ChatReady`) -- add `isOffline` + `copyWith`.
- `lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_state.dart:108-144` (`ChatUiMessage`) -- add `serverId` + `copyWith`/`==`/`hashCode`/`toString`.
- `lib/features/chat/domain/repositories/chat_repository.dart:53-56` -- add `retryMessage(sessionId, userMessageId)`.
- `lib/features/chat/data/repositories/chat_repository_impl.dart:116-122` (`sendMessage`) -- sibling `retryMessage` passthrough.
- `lib/features/chat/data/datasources/chat_remote_data_source.dart:137-271` -- extract shared SSE buffer/parse helper; add `retryMessage` hitting `chat-messages-retry`, `pathParams: [sessionId, userMessageId]`, `data: const {}`.
- `lib/features/chat/domain/services/connectivity_watcher.dart` (new) -- `abstract class ConnectivityWatcher { Stream<bool> watch(); }`, mirrors `mic_recorder.dart`.
- `lib/features/chat/data/services/connectivity_plus_watcher.dart` (new) -- `connectivity_plus` impl.
- `lib/features/chat/chat_injection.dart:32-53` -- register `ConnectivityWatcher`; inject into `ChatCubit` (line 50-51).
- `lib/core/network/retry_interceptor.dart:36-39` -- add `'chat-messages-retry'`.
- `lib/features/chat/presentation/widgets/chat_bubble.dart:17-24,126-143` -- add `onRetry` callback; tappable region, min 44pt, `Semantics(button: true)`.
- `lib/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen.dart:181-189` -- wire `onRetry: () => cubit.retryMessage(messages[index].id)`.
- `lib/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen.dart:148-150` -- insert offline banner (`state is ChatReady && state.isOffline`).
- `lib/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen.dart:304` -- `canSend` += `!state.isOffline`.
- `lib/core/widgets/app_drawer.dart:73-77` -- gate "Novo Chat" on `!isOffline` via `BlocBuilder`.
- `pubspec.yaml` -- add via `fvm flutter pub add connectivity_plus`.
- `test/features/chat/**`, `test/core/widgets/app_drawer_test.dart` -- extend per the I/O matrix; reuse `test/core/navigation/app_router_test.dart:128-156`'s `_FakeChatRepository`; add a fake `ConnectivityWatcher`.

## Tasks & Acceptance

**Execution:**
- [x] `chat/domain/services/connectivity_watcher.dart`, `chat/data/services/connectivity_plus_watcher.dart` -- create the abstraction + impl.
- [x] `chat/presentation/cubit/chat_state.dart` -- `ChatReady.isOffline`, `ChatUiMessage.serverId`.
- [x] `chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit.dart` -- connectivity subscription, `serverId` capture, `retryMessage`.
- [x] `chat/domain/repositories/chat_repository.dart`, `data/repositories/chat_repository_impl.dart`, `data/datasources/chat_remote_data_source.dart` -- `retryMessage` through all three layers.
- [x] `chat/chat_injection.dart` -- wire `ConnectivityWatcher` into DI and `ChatCubit`.
- [x] `core/network/retry_interceptor.dart` -- exclude `chat-messages-retry` from transparent retry.
- [x] `chat/presentation/widgets/chat_bubble.dart`, `presentation/screens/chat_screen.dart`, `core/widgets/app_drawer.dart` -- tap-to-retry UI, offline banner, composer lock, "Novo Chat" disable.
- [x] Extend the test files listed in the Code Map per the I/O matrix.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given a dropped/failed AI response, when I tap its retry copy, then the same bubble regenerates in place, with no new question bubble and no re-send of the question.
- Given I'm offline, when Home/Chat is open, then the composer is disabled with the offline banner visible, while history stays fully visible and scrollable.
- Given I'm offline, when I open the side menu, then "Novo Chat" is disabled.
- Given connectivity returns, when `isOffline` flips back, then the composer and "Novo Chat" re-enable automatically.

## Spec Change Log

## Design Notes

- `serverId` (not reusing `id`) avoids ever swapping a `ChatUiMessage.id` mid-stream — `id` stays the stable lookup key; `serverId` is only the value sent to `chat-messages-retry`.
- `ConnectivityWatcher` lives in `chat/domain/services/`, not `core/`, since no other feature needs connectivity yet; promote it later if one does.

## Verification

**Commands:**
- `fvm flutter pub get` -- expected: resolves with `connectivity_plus` added, no conflicts

  - **Missing verification:** Any assertion that `ConnectivityPlusWatcher.watch()`/`_isOnline` correctly maps a `List<ConnectivityResult>` (or a `checkConnectivity()`/`onConnectivityChanged` emission) to the right boolean.
  - **Demonstration:** The class's own constructor already accepts an injectable `Connectivity?` (built specifically to allow substituting a fake/mock), yet nothing uses that seam.   - **Suggested test shape:** A small unit test for `ConnectivityPlusWatcher` passing a mock/fake `Connectivity` (mocktail `Mock implements Connectivity`, stubbing `checkConnectivity()` and `onConnectivityChanged`) and asserting `watch()` emits the expected booleans for representative `ConnectivityResult` lists (e.g. `[wifi]` -> `true`, `[none]` -> `false`), plus the best-effort initial-read-failure path.
  
  ## Other findings
  
  - `lib/core/widgets/app_drawer.dart:83-90` wraps "Novo Chat" in its own `BlocBuilder<ChatCubit, ChatState>` with no `buildWhen`, so — same as the pre-existing "CONVERSAS" `BlocBuilder` already flagged in this project's own deferred-work log — this second drawer `BlocBuilder` now also rebuilds on every `ChatReady` emission (including once per streamed AI token) even while the drawer is closed and off-screen.   Everything else I traced — the `listSessions()`/`listMessages()` "all items malformed → Left" fix, the `_cachedSessions()` `DateTime.tryParse` fix, the `switchSession()`/`startNewSession()` stale-`isSending` fix, the new `retryMessage` flow (normal retry, no-`serverId` fallback, second-failure-stays-tappable, no-op guards, offline composer lock/banner, "Novo Chat" gating) — has a test that actually drives the changed branch and asserts the changed output, at the cubit, repository, datasource, or widget level as appropriate. I did not find a missing-adoption gap: `startNewSession`/`retryMessage` each have exactly one call site in `lib/`, both already wired to the new behavior.
</agent-message>

entries.name: SendMessage
entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.

input.message:
Three parallel review layers (blind-hunter, edge-case-hunter, verification-gap) just reviewed the full diff of your spec-6-3 implementation. After triage, 8 findings need patching now (no spec change, no revert — just fixes). Apply all 8, then re-run `fvm flutter analyze` (expect zero issues) and `fvm flutter test` (expect all passing), and fix anything that breaks. Report back when done.

1. `lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit.dart` — `sendMessage()`/`retryMessage()` never check `current.isOffline`. The offline lock today is UI-only (`_ChatComposer.canSend`), but a failed bubble's retry tap is a separate affordance not gated by that `canSend` check — a user can tap "tentar novamente" on a past failed bubble while the offline banner is showing and trigger a real network call, contradicting the banner's own "novas mensagens bloqueadas" copy. Add an early-return guard (mirroring the existing `current is! ChatReady`/`_isSending` guards) so neither method proceeds while `current.isOffline` is true.

2. `lib/features/chat/presentation/widgets/chat_bubble.dart` — the failed-bubble's `Semantics(button: true, ...)` is hardcoded regardless of whether the nullable `onRetry` callback was actually supplied. Gate it on `onRetry != null` so a bubble built without a retry callback isn't announced to screen readers as a working button.

3. `lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit.dart` — `retryMessage()`'s guard checks `messages[aiIndex].status == ChatMessageStatus.failed` but never checks `role == ChatMessageRole.assistant`. Not reachable today (only AI messages ever get `failed` status), but add the role check anyway for defensive correctness, matching this codebase's existing defensive-guard style.

4. `lib/features/chat/presentation/widgets/chat_bubble.dart` — the retry copy string `'Falha ao gerar resposta — toque para tentar novamente'` is duplicated verbatim in both the `Semantics.label` and the `Text` child. Extract it to one shared local constant/variable used by both, so a future copy edit can't desync the spoken label from the visible text.

5. `pubspec.yaml` — `connectivity_plus` was added with no explanatory comment, inconsistent with this file's own convention of commenting every dependency choice (e.g. the existing comment block right above it explaining why `path_provider` must be a direct dependency). Add a short comment explaining why it's there (feature-local `ConnectivityWatcher` impl for story 6.3's offline composer lock).

6. Add a widget-level test (in `test/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen_test.dart` or `test/features/chat/presentation/widgets/chat_bubble_test.dart`, whichever fits your existing structure) exercising the *normal* retry path — a failed AI bubble whose preceding user message has a `serverId` — driven through an actual `ChatBubble` tap inside a mounted `ChatScreen`/widget tree, asserting `chat-messages-retry` ends up called (not the `sendMessage` fallback). Today that path is only covered at the `ChatCubit` unit-test level; the widget-level retry test you wrote only covers the no-`serverId` fallback. (Direct precedent: spec-6-2's own round-1 review treated an identical "AC verified only at the cubit, not the screen, layer" gap as a Patch.)

7. Add a unit test for `lib/features/chat/data/services/connectivity_plus_watcher.dart`'s online/offline mapping, using a mocked/faked `Connectivity` (its constructor already accepts an injectable `Connectivity?` — use that seam). Assert representative `ConnectivityResult` lists map to the correct boolean (e.g. `[wifi]` -> `true`, `[none]` -> `false`). Right now every test that exercises `ChatReady.isOffline` goes through `FakeConnectivityWatcher`, so this file's actual mapping logic — the only adapter wired into the real app via DI — has zero coverage; an inverted comparison there would ship with the full suite green.

8. `lib/features/chat/data/services/connectivity_plus_watcher.dart` — `watch()`'s leading `await _connectivity.checkConnectivity()` has no timeout and runs before the generator ever reaches the live `onConnectivityChanged` subscription. If that platform-channel call hangs instead of throwing, connectivity watching never starts at all for the rest of the session (not just a missed initial snapshot). Restructure so a hang/slow response in that initial read can't block the live subscription from starting (e.g. race it with a short timeout that falls through to subscribing anyway, or start the `onConnectivityChanged` subscription first and treat the initial check as a best-effort seed value only).

Everything else from the review (two new `BlocBuilder`s with no `buildWhen`, the no-`serverId` fallback giving no UI hint it resent as a new message, `isOffline` defaulting false until the first connectivity reading lands, the offline banner not covering the bootstrap-loading/error states) was triaged as defer — I'm logging those to deferred-work.md myself, no action needed from you on those.

# Step 5: Present

## RULES

- **Language** — Speak in `English`. Write any file output in `English`.
- NEVER auto-push.

## INSTRUCTIONS

### Generate Suggested Review Order

Read `{baseline_commit}` from `{spec_file}` frontmatter and construct the diff of all changes since that commit.

Append the review order as a `## Suggested Review Order` section to `{spec_file}` **after the last existing section**. Do not modify the Code Map.

Build the trail as an ordered sequence of **stops** — clickable `path:line` references with brief framing — optimized for a human reviewer reading top-down to understand the change:

1. **Order by concern, not by file.** Group stops by the conceptual concern they address (e.g., "validation logic", "schema change", "UI binding"). A single file may appear under multiple concerns.
2. **Lead with the entry point** — the single highest-leverage file:line a reviewer should look at first to grasp the design intent.
3. **Inside each concern**, order stops from most important / architecturally interesting to supporting. Lightly bias toward higher-risk or boundary-crossing stops.
4. **End with peripherals** — tests, config, types, and other supporting changes come last.
5. **Every code reference is a clickable spec-file-relative link.** Compute each link target as a relative path from `{spec_file}`'s directory to the changed file. Format each stop as a markdown link: `[short-name:line](../../path/to/file.ts#L42)`. Use a `#L` line anchor. Use the file's basename (or shortest unambiguous suffix) plus line number as the link text. The relative path must be dynamically derived — never hardcode the depth.
6. **Each stop gets one ultra-concise line of framing** (≤15 words) — why this approach was chosen here and what it achieves in the context of the change. No paragraphs.

Format each stop as framing first, link on the next indented line:

```markdown
## Suggested Review Order

**{Concern name}**

- {one-line framing}
  [`file.ts:42`](../../src/path/to/file.ts#L42)

- {one-line framing}
  [`other.ts:17`](../../src/path/to/other.ts#L17)

**{Next concern}**

- {one-line framing}
  [`file.ts:88`](../../src/path/to/file.ts#L88)
```

> The `../../` prefix above is illustrative — compute the actual relative path from `{spec_file}`'s directory to each target file.

When there is only one concern, omit the bold label — just list the stops directly.

Change `{spec_file}` status to `done` in the frontmatter.

If version control is available and the tree is dirty, create a local commit with a conventional message derived from the spec title.

Run `code -r "{project-root}" "{spec_file}"` — the repository root first so VS Code opens in the right context, then the spec file. title: 'Story 6.3 — Dropped-Stream Resilience & Offline Composer Lock'
type: 'feature'
created: '2026-11-05'
status: 'in-review'
review_loop_iteration: 0
baseline_commit: '43351cf59fa0a85125a5d50eefbe984600c7b403'
context: ['{project-root}/_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/epic-6-context.md']

<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">

## Intent

**Problem:** A dropped/failed AI response is marked `failed` with no retry path — `ChatCubit` has none. The composer has no offline-awareness either; `_ChatComposer`'s own doc (`chat_screen.dart:284-288`) names this gap as "Story 6.3's job," and no connectivity detection exists anywhere in the app.

**Approach:** Add `ChatCubit.retryMessage`, backed by a new `ChatRepository.retryMessage`/`ChatRemoteDataSource.retryMessage` mirroring `sendMessage`'s SSE consumption against `chat-messages-retry`. Add a feature-local `ConnectivityWatcher` (domain service, `connectivity_plus` impl) that `ChatCubit` consumes into a new `ChatReady.isOffline` flag, gating the composer, a new offline banner, and the drawer's "Novo Chat".

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- Tap-to-retry renders only on a `failed` AI bubble — copy "Falha ao gerar resposta — toque para tentar novamente" (`cerne-prototype.html`), replacing `chat_bubble.dart:136-141`; tappable, 44pt min (`DesignTokens.insertionModalTapTargetMin`), `Semantics(button: true)`.
- Retry resets the *same* bubble (id, position) to `streaming`/empty, then reuses `_applyStreamEvent`/`_markFailed` (`chat_cubit.dart:358-421`) unchanged — never a second bubble, never a duplicate question.
- Retry is keyed by the user message's persisted id, captured from `message_created` (currently a no-op, `chat_cubit.dart:366-371`). Add `ChatUiMessage.serverId`: from `_fromDomain` (`chat_cubit.dart:251-256`, `= message.id`) and, for an in-session send, from `message_created`'s `userMessageId`.
- `ConnectivityWatcher`: feature-local domain service (`chat/domain/services/`) + `connectivity_plus` impl (`chat/data/services/`), injected into `ChatCubit`'s ctor — mirrors `MicRecorder`'s domain/data split (`lib/features/capture/domain/services/mic_recorder.dart`), never through `ChatRepository`.
- `ChatReady` gains `isOffline` (default `false`), driving: `_ChatComposer.canSend` (`chat_screen.dart:304`, text+send only — "+" stays tappable); an offline banner between `_ChatHeader` and the list (`chat_screen.dart:148-150`), copy "Sem conexão — histórico disponível, novas mensagens bloqueadas", `Icons.wifi_off`, `DesignTokens.colorInfoOffline`/`colorOnPrimary` (existing tokens); `AppDrawer`'s "Novo Chat" (`app_drawer.dart:73-77`, disabled + dimmed).
- Add `'chat-messages-retry'` to `RetryInterceptor.neverRetriedFunctions` (`retry_interceptor.dart:36-39`).

**Ask First:** none identified.

**Never:**
- Changing `ChatRepositoryImpl`'s existing reactive `Failure.networkOffline` handling — `isOffline` is additive only.
- Calling `chat-messages-retry` with no `serverId` (stream dropped before `message_created`) — falls back to a full `sendMessage` resend of the same content into the same bubble slot.
- A second retry while one is in flight — reuses `_isSending` verbatim.
- Disabling the "+" when offline, or removing `AppDrawer._startNewSession`'s offline `SnackBar` (spec-6-2) — both stay.

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| Tap retry, normal | Failed AI bubble; preceding user message has `serverId` | Bubble resets to `streaming`/empty, fills via `chat-messages-retry`'s SSE, ends `complete` | A second failure re-marks `failed`, stays tappable |
| Tap retry, no `serverId` | Stream dropped before `message_created` arrived | Falls back to `sendMessage`, same content, same slot | Same handling as any send |
| Goes offline mid-session | `ConnectivityWatcher` emits `false` | Composer + "Novo Chat" disable, banner appears, history stays scrollable | N/A |
| Comes back online | `ConnectivityWatcher` emits `true` | Banner disappears, composer + "Novo Chat" re-enable | N/A |

</frozen-after-approval>

## Code Map

- `lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit.dart:18` (ctor) -- add `ConnectivityWatcher` param; subscribe, store `_isOffline`, emit on `ChatReady` when it changes.
- `lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit.dart:313-317` (`sendMessage` `onData`) -- on `ChatMessageCreatedEvent`, set `userMessage.serverId` before `_applyStreamEvent`.
- `lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit.dart:251-256` (`_fromDomain`) -- `serverId: message.id`.
- `lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit.dart:274-341` (`sendMessage`) -- mirror for new `retryMessage(aiMessageId)`: same guards, find target + preceding user message's `serverId`, reset content/status, subscribe (`retryMessage` or `sendMessage` fallback), reuse `_applyStreamEvent`/`_markFailed`/`_finishSending`.
- `lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_state.dart:41-98` (`ChatReady`) -- add `isOffline` + `copyWith`.
- `lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_state.dart:108-144` (`ChatUiMessage`) -- add `serverId` + `copyWith`/`==`/`hashCode`/`toString`.
- `lib/features/chat/domain/repositories/chat_repository.dart:53-56` -- add `retryMessage(sessionId, userMessageId)`.
- `lib/features/chat/data/repositories/chat_repository_impl.dart:116-122` (`sendMessage`) -- sibling `retryMessage` passthrough.

- `lib/features/chat/domain/services/connectivity_watcher.dart` (new) -- `abstract class ConnectivityWatcher { Stream<bool> watch(); }`, mirrors `mic_recorder.dart`.
- `lib/features/chat/data/services/connectivity_plus_watcher.dart` (new) -- `connectivity_plus` impl.

- `lib/core/network/retry_interceptor.dart:36-39` -- add `'chat-messages-retry'`.
- `lib/features/chat/presentation/widgets/chat_bubble.dart:17-24,126-143` -- add `onRetry` callback; tappable region, min 44pt, `Semantics(button: true)`.

## Tasks & Acceptance

**Execution:**
- [x] `chat/domain/services/connectivity_watcher.dart`, `chat/data/services/connectivity_plus_watcher.dart` -- create the abstraction + impl.
- [x] `chat/presentation/cubit/chat_state.dart` -- `ChatReady.isOffline`, `ChatUiMessage.serverId`.
- [x] `chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit.dart` -- connectivity subscription, `serverId` capture, `retryMessage`.
- [x] `chat/domain/repositories/chat_repository.dart`, `data/repositories/chat_repository_impl.dart`, `data/datasources/chat_remote_data_source.dart` -- `retryMessage` through all three layers.

- [x] Extend the test files listed in the Code Map per the I/O matrix.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given a dropped/failed AI response, when I tap its retry copy, then the same bubble regenerates in place, with no new question bubble and no re-send of the question.
- Given I'm offline, when Home/Chat is open, then the composer is disabled with the offline banner visible, while history stays fully visible and scrollable.
- Given I'm offline, when I open the side menu, then "Novo Chat" is disabled.
- Given connectivity returns, when `isOffline` flips back, then the composer and "Novo Chat" re-enable automatically.

## Design Notes

- `serverId` (not reusing `id`) avoids ever swapping a `ChatUiMessage.id` mid-stream — `id` stays the stable lookup key; `serverId` is only the value sent to `chat-messages-retry`.
- `ConnectivityWatcher` lives in `chat/domain/services/`, not `core/`, since no other feature needs connectivity yet; promote it later if one does.

+- Excludes the new endpoint from transparent interceptor-level retry — same non-idempotent-POST rationale as `chat-messages-send`.
+- Tap-to-retry UI — the exact prototype copy, deduped into one constant, `Semantics(button:true)` only when `onRetry` is actually wired.
+- The feature-local connectivity port — mirrors `MicRecorder`'s domain/data split, never routed through `ChatRepository`.

+- `connectivity_plus` impl — live `onConnectivityChanged` subscription starts immediately; the initial `checkConnectivity()` read is a non-blocking best-effort seed (review fix: a hang there can no longer stall live updates).
+- Folds each reading into `_isOffline`, re-emitting it onto the current `ChatReady` — the one place the signal enters cubit state.
+- `ChatReady.isOffline` — the field every UI gate below reads.
+- Composer text field + send icon disable — the "+" stays tappable regardless.
+- The offline banner, docked above the message list.
+- DI wiring — the one real `Connectivity`/`ConnectivityWatcher` registration feeding `ChatCubit`.
+- Unit coverage for the real adapter's online/offline mapping and hang-safety — the one thing every other test bypasses via the fake.
+- Shared controllable fake used everywhere else `ChatCubit` is constructed directly.
